arxiv-2012-12902.title: BlackHawk: A tool for computing Black Hole evaporation
arxiv-2012-12902.creator: Alexandre Arbey
arxiv-2012-12902.description: Abstract We present the public code BlackHawk, a powerful tool to compute the evaporation of any distribution of Schwarzschild and Kerr Black Holes and the emission spectra of Hawking radiation. [a]Jérémy Auffinger 1 Introduction The nature of dark matter (DM) is a long standing problem in modern cosmology.

arxiv-2107-06092.title: Search for exotic decays of the Higgs boson into long-lived particles in p ​ p pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV using displaced vertices in the ATLAS inner detector
arxiv-2107-06092.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2107-06092.description: Abstract A novel search for exotic decays of the Higgs boson into pairs of long-lived neutral particles, each decaying into a bottom quark pair, is performed using 139 fb -1 of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV proton–proton collision data collected with the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

arxiv-2209-04662.title: CosmoGridV1: a simulated 𝒘 ​ 𝐂𝐃𝐌 w\rm{CDM} theory prediction for map-level cosmological inference
arxiv-2209-04662.creator: Joachim Stadel
arxiv-2209-04662.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Joachim Stadel. We present CosmoGridV1 : a large set of lightcone simulations for map-level cosmological inference with probes of large scale structure. It is designed for cosmological parameter measurement based on Stage-III photometric surveys with non-Gaussian statistics and machine learning.

arxiv-2301-03477.title: Bridging High-Density, Electron Beam Coronal Transport and Deep Chromospheric Heating in Stellar Flares
arxiv-2301-03477.creator: Adam F. Kowalski
arxiv-2301-03477.description: Abstract The optical and near-ultraviolet (NUV) continuum radiation in M dwarf flares is thought to be the impulsive response of the lower stellar atmosphere to magnetic energy release and electron acceleration at coronal altitudes. This radiation is sometimes interpreted as evidence of a thermal photospheric spectrum with T ≈ 10 4 T\approx 10^{4} K.

arxiv-2310-20371.title: Optimal work fluctuations for thermally isolated systems in weak processes
arxiv-2310-20371.creator: Pierre Nazé
arxiv-2310-20371.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Pierre Nazé. The fluctuation-dissipation relation for the classical definition of work is extended to thermally isolated systems, in classical and quantum realms. From this, the optimal work variance is calculated, showing it achieves its minimum possible value, independent of the rate of the process, in a so-called quasistatic variance, related to the difference between the quasistatic work and the difference of Helmholtz’s free energy of the system.

Park was partially supported by NSF grant DMS-1855536, and G. Panova was partially supported by the NSF grant DMS-1939717.
arxiv-2311-09209.creator: Alejandro H. Morales, Greta Panova, GaYee Park
arxiv-2311-09209.description: Abstract . Standard tableaux of skew shape are fundamental objects in enumerative and algebraic combinatorics and no product formula for the number is known. In 2014, Naruse gave a formula (NHLF) as a positive sum over excited diagrams of products of hook-lengths.

arxiv-2312-03107.title: Short-lived repeating fast radio bursts from tidal disruption of white dwarfs by intermediate-mass black holes Short-lived repeating fast radio bursts from tidal disruption of white dwarfs by intermediate-mass black holes –
arxiv-2312-03107.creator: Jing-Tong Xing, Tong Liu
arxiv-2312-03107.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jing-Tong Xing, Tong Liu. The origin of repeating fast radio bursts (RFRBs) is still a mystery. We propose that short-lived RFRBs might be triggered from the tidal disruption of white dwarfs (WDs) by intermediate-mass black holes (BHs). In this model, we show that the remnant WD clusters after tidal collapse cuts the magnetic lines on the BH accretion discs, and during each fall of the clump, so that electrons are torn from the surface of the mass and instantly accelerated to the relativistic energy.

arxiv-2410-06417.title: A multi-channel silicon package for large-scale skipper-CCD experiments
arxiv-2410-06417.creator: A. M. Botti, C. Chavez, M. Sofo-Haro, C. S. Miller, F. Chierchie, M. Jonas, M. Lisovenko, H. Gutti, D. Czaplewski, A. Lathrop, L. Scott, J. Tiffenberg, G. Fernandez-Moroni, J. Estrada
arxiv-2410-06417.description: Abstract The next generation of experiments for light-dark-matter and neutrino searches based on skipper Charge Coupled Devices (skipper-CCDs) introduces new challenges for the sensor packaging and readout architecture. Scaling the active mass while simultaneously reducing the experimental backgrounds in orders of magnitude requires a novel high-density silicon-based package that must be massively produced and tested.

arxiv-2411-18392.title: The more, the better? Evaluating the role of EEG preprocessing for deep learning applications.
arxiv-2411-18392.creator: Federico Del Pup, Andrea Zanola, Louis Fabrice Tshimanga, Alessandra Bertoldo, Manfredo Atzori
arxiv-2411-18392.description: Abstract The last decade has witnessed a notable surge in deep learning applications for the analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) data, thanks to its demonstrated superiority over conventional statistical techniques. However, even deep learning models can underperform if trained with bad processed data.

arxiv-2507-01178.title: Diffusion Explorer : Interactive Exploration of Diffusion Models
arxiv-2507-01178.creator: Alec Helbling Georgia Tech, Polo Chau Georgia Tech
arxiv-2507-01178.description: Abstract Diffusion models have been central to the development of recent image, video, and even text generation systems. They posses striking geometric properties that can be faithfully portrayed in low-dimensional settings. However, existing resources for explaining diffusion either require an advanced theoretical foundation or focus on their neural network architectures rather than their rich geometric properties.

arxiv-2601-19220.title: Accelerated Multiple Wasserstein Gradient Flows for Multi-objective Distributional Optimization
arxiv-2601-19220.creator: Dai Hai Nguyen, Dung Duc Nguyen, Atsuyoshi Nakamura, Hiroshi Mamitsuka
arxiv-2601-19220.description: Abstract We study multi-objective optimization over probability distributions in Wasserstein space. Recently, 8 introduced Multiple Wasserstein Gradient Descent (MWGraD) algorithm, which exploits the geometric structure of Wasserstein space to jointly optimize multiple objectives. Building on this approach, we propose an accelerated variant, A-MWGraD, inspired by Nesterov’s acceleration.

arxiv-2602-22782.title: Most probably trangle-free graphs
arxiv-2602-22782.creator: Yuhang Bai, Gyula O.H. Katona, Zixuan Yang, [2mm] School of Mathematics, Statistics Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi’an, Shaanxi, P.R. China
arxiv-2602-22782.description: Abstract The celebrated Mantel’s theorem states that any triangle-free graph on n n vertices contains at most ⌊ n 2 / 4 ⌋ \left\lfloor n^{2}/4\right\rfloor edges. It is natural to ask how many triangles must exist in a graph with more than ⌊ n 2 / 4 ⌋ \left\lfloor n^{2}/4\right\rfloor edges–a problem known as the Erdős-Rademacher problem.

pmc-10691416.title: RELIGIOSITY AND DEATH ANXIETY AMONG CANCER PATIENTS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF RELIGIOUS COMFORT AND STRUGGLE
pmc-10691416.creator: Radosław Rybarski, Rafał P Bartczuk, Jacek Śliwak, Beata Zarzycka
pmc-10691416.description: Objectives:Religiosity may serve as a personal source of support when people face a life-threatening illness, but it can also elicit stress. The main aim of this study is to show how various religious dimensions interplay in predicting death anxiety in patients diagnosed as having cancer.

pmc-10696062.title: Metagenomic sequencing detects human respiratory and enteric viruses in air samples collected from congregate settings
pmc-10696062.creator: Nicholas R Minor, Mitchell D Ramuta, Miranda R Stauss, Olivia E Harwood, Savannah F Brakefield, Alexandra Alberts, William C Vuyk, Max J Bobholz, Jenna R Rosinski, Sydney Wolf, Madelyn Lund, Madison Mussa, Lucas J Beversdorf, Matthew T Aliota, Shelby L O’Connor, David H O’Connor

Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, environmental surveillance strategies, including wastewater and air sampling, have been used alongside widespread individual-based SARS-CoV-2 testing programs to provide population-level data.

pmc-11539083.title: Necrotising cellulitis occurring after cosmetic blepharoplasty: A case report
pmc-11539083.creator: Rhyme Timoumi, Laura Moyal, Jean-Philippe Nordmann, Amin Bennedjai
pmc-11539083.description: SummaryPeriorbital necrotising cellulitis is a rare localisation of fasciitis and an exceptional complication of cosmetic blepharoplasty.We discuss here the case of a 52-year-old woman who presented with orbital cellulitis 2 days after undergoing a bilateral cosmetic lower blepharoplasty. The diagnosis was confirmed on magnetic resonance imaging.

pmc-11658393.title: Risk factors of severe conditions in hospitalized children with adenovirus infection and chest CT features
pmc-11658393.creator: Shaofang Wang, Shichao Kang, Lili Guo, Shuchang Zhou, Yanjie Zhao, Huifen Shen, Shourui Jin, Hanxiong Guan, Liming Xia, Qiongjie Hu
pmc-11658393.description: BackgroundChildren infected with human adenovirus (HAdV) were at particularly high risk of developing severe disease, but the risk factors of severe conditions are poorly understood.ObjectivesTo explore the risk factors for developing into severe conditions in pediatric patients with HAdV infection by analyzing baseline epidemiological data, clinical characteristics, and computed tomography (CT) imaging features.

pmc-12495669.title: Vitamin C supplementation to pregnant smokers alters asthma- and allergy-associated CpGs in child buccal DNA at 5 years of age
pmc-12495669.creator: Lyndsey E Shorey-Kendrick, Cindy T McEvoy, Kristin Milner, Julia Harris, Julie Brownsberger, Robert S Tepper, Byung Park, Lina Gao, Annette Vu, Cynthia D Morris, Emma E Thompson, Carole Ober, Eliot R Spindel
pmc-12495669.description: BackgroundWe previously reported improved respiratory outcomes in babies born to pregnant smokers supplemented with vitamin C (500 mg/day) versus placebo in a randomized clinical trial. Improved respiratory outcomes persisted to 5 years of age and were associated with buccal DNA methylation (DNAm) measured using the InfiniumMethylationEPIC array.

pmc-12719475.title: Rapid-onset methimazole-induced lupus in a pediatric patient with Graves’ disease: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-12719475.creator: Nouraldeen Deeb, Salahaldeen Deeb, Mohammad Badawi, Mohammad Alfrookh, Bashar Douden, Saed I. Atawnah
pmc-12719475.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Graves’ disease (GD) is the leading cause of autoimmune hyperthyroidism, though pediatric cases are uncommon. Methimazole (MMI) is the first-line therapy; however, drug-induced lupus erythematosus (DILE) secondary to MMI is rare and may be overlooked. We report the case of a 16-year-old girl with newly diagnosed GD who developed inflammatory polyarthritis, a diffuse pruritic maculopapular rash, and alopecia within 1 week of starting MMI (10 mg/day).

pmc-12727188.title: Associations between temporomandibular disorders/bruxism and head and neck pains: a bidirectional Mendelian randomization study
pmc-12727188.creator: Shan-Shan Du, Yuan-Yuan Hu, Yu-Ming Niu
pmc-12727188.description: Background: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) and bruxism are the most common disorders affecting the oral and maxillofacial system. Patients with TMDs or bruxism frequently suffer from chronic head and neck pains (HNPs); however, the etiology between TMDs/bruxism and HNPs remains unclear.

pmc-13280295.title: Risankizumab versus Deucravacitinib in Adults With Moderate Plaque Psoriasis: 16-Week Results from the Phase 4 IMMpactful Trial
pmc-13280295.creator: Nina Magnolo, Jennifer Soung, John Frew, Antonio Costanzo, Hiram Ruiz-Santiago, Kilian Eyerich, Mar Llamas-Velasco, Michael Bukhalo, Raja K Sivamani, Angela Moore, Tianshuang Wu, Jiaheng Xie, Manish Patel, Doug Ashley, Blair Kaplan, Vassilis Stakias, Ramon Espaillat, Richard B Warren
pmc-13280295.description: IntroductionRisankizumab (RZB) and deucravacitinib (DEU) are both approved for the treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Physicians value head-to-head comparisons between available therapies to make evidence-based treatment decisions. This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of RZB compared with DEU for the treatment of patients with moderate psoriasis who have not previously received biologic treatment.
